articles.title: PM widens fuel subsidy, eases weekly limits
articles.description: • Token validity increased, people can now use Rs500 discount per week • Minister says scheme benefits 24m • Sindh likely to introduce revised market timings ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday approved a revised structure for the public under the fuel relief scheme currently in vogue across the country, expanding it to include more two- and three-wheelers, and easing weekly limits to offer motorists more flexibility in how they use the support. The prime minister, who is currently abroad on an official visit, directed that motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi rickshaws up to 20 years old should also be included in the scheme. “All motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi rickshaws registered on or after January 1, 2006, will be eligible for registration under the fuel relief scheme,” a press release issued by the Prime Minister’s Office said. In addition, two- and three-wheelers can now benefit from a concession of Rs500 in one week without quantity limits. According to details, where each token previously entitled the holder to five litres of fuel, now people will be able to obtain a token that entitles them to a Rs500 discount. Each token remains valid for a period of seven days from issuance. Eligible citizens will now be able to avail a maximum concession of Rs2,000 per month, through multiple token redemptions According to Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, around 24 million people are currently benefitting from the fuel relief scheme. Addressing a press conference, the minister detailed steps being taken to ensure that the subsidy scheme is implemented smoothly, saying that parliamentarians and political teams were assisting citizens through facilitation camps that had been formed across the four provinces, as well as Gilgit-Baltistan, AJK and Islamabad. Mr Chaudhry said he had personally visited several facilitation camps in the capital, which were being approached by a large number of people, whose feedback and complaints were being conveyed directly to the teams supervising the package. The minister conceded that some initial issues had emerged in the implementation of the scheme, particularly regarding the payment mechanism for petrol pump owners, but these had been resolved after meetings with the All Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association. Talking about the austerity measures imposed by the Centre, he said they were meant to reduce government expenditure. Except for vehicles engaged in operational field activities and those of the defence services, fuel allocations for government vehicles had been reduced by 50 per cent, he said. Mr Chaudhry also said that restrictions had also been imposed on new purchases of government vehicles and other items, while official dinners and lunches had been curtailed. He added official foreign trips would not be government-sponsored, and where an official trip was necessary, economy-class travel would be used. Meanwhile, the provinces showed little movement on the question of austerity measures on Friday. Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa seem to still be mulling the measures. However, a senior Sindh government official told Dawn that the decision to revise market and restaurant closure timings in line with the federal government notification is likely to be announced next week. “The government does not want early closure [of markets] this weekend to facilitate traders,” he added. Azfar-ul-Ashfaque in Karachi also contributed to this report Published in Dawn, September 19th, 2026

articles.title: Canadian leader Carney lauds plans for EU alliance following US tariffs
articles.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has returned from Europe and cast Canada as moving quickly beyond its historic reliance on the United States. His comments come after a whirlwind week in which he embraced the prospect of becoming the European Union’s first associate member. Carney says Canada and Europe had “launched a process for a new alliance.” He also called the latest U.S. tariffs a “miscalculation” and repeated that suspending trade talks with Washington last month was the right decision. A day earlier, Carney told the European Parliament that Canada needed more markets and partners so no country could control its economy, impair its sovereignty or constrain its choices.

articles.title: Why is Meta’s Threads being flooded with eerily identical investment advice?
articles.description: In a normal context, the phrase “my husband and I work for JPMorgan” might be merely a not-so-subtle flex. But lately on Threads, it’s seems more like a telltale sign that the user is in fact a bot. Users on Meta’s short-form social network have recently noticed a barrage of strange recurring posts, all following a template that begins with phrases like “my husband and I” or “my wife and I,” followed by claims to work for companies like Exxon, Fidelity, IBM, and many, many more. Below the post, investment advice follows the phrase “I’m only going to say this once,” with a list of various tickers and instructions, such as “don’t buy” or “buy at” pasted below. In one case, a post read , “My husband and I are both analysts at PepsiCo, I’ll only say this once. My advice for September 20th is: cancel your plans and stay home.” Another similar post simply switched the date and company. “My husband and I are both analysts at Expedia Group. I’ll only say this once. My advice October 20th is cancel your plans and stay home,” the post read. But in both cases, the investment advice was the same: eight tickers listed in the same order, each with a purchase instruction by its side. “$TSLA (Tesla) — Don’t buy $PLTR (Palantir) — Don’t buy $ARM (Arm) — Don’t buy $NVDA (Nvidia) — Buy at $223–$225 $AMZN (Amazon) — Buy at $265–$267 $AVGO (Broadcom) — Buy at $415–$417 $SOFI (SoFi) — Buy at $17–$18 $RKLB (Rocket Lab) — Buy at $80–$81′′ One of the posts also included a screenshot of what looks like a Wells Fargo account dashboard, listing the balance at $32.5 million as apparent proof of the user’s financial success. This habit appears to be widespread with many other posts sharing similar screenshots from various banks, all at around the $30 million mark. What’s going on with these posts? The bizarre posts are easy to find on Threads by simply searching for “my husband and I,” with dozens of posts surfacing from minutes, to days, to even weeks ago. The phenomenon appears to be unique to Threads, as such posts were not widespread on other apps like Bluesky and X, based on a cursory search conducted by Fast Company on Friday. Fast Company reached out to Meta for comment. We will update this story if we receive additional details about what’s happening. Meanwhile, many users have taken to poking fun at the strange recurring posts, whose robotic and repeated nature has led users to believe that they are generated by bots. “My wife and I both work at the Wonka factory. I’m only going to say this once. My advice for February 31st is to cancel your plans and stay home,” a user said on Threads. Another responded , “How can I take this seriously without a screenshot of your bank balance?” But many more are speculating on the origins and intentions of the alleged bot messages, with some users believing that the posts are meant to be a market manipulation tactic. “It’s micro pushing of stocks,” one user said on Threads, speculating that the activity could be an attempt to game tools that use AI as part of their stock analyses. “I think the bot farms might have caught onto something . . . The pattern might be extremely obvious to humans but not so to an AI.”
